description: Synthetic test/demo data only. These documents are not official SACCO policies.

documents.title: Test Demo: Compound Interest
documents.content: Compound interest is interest calculated on the original amount and on interest accumulated from earlier periods. This test explanation is synthetic and exists only to verify semantic retrieval.

documents.title: Test Demo: Loan Repayment
documents.content: Loan repayment means returning borrowed money through scheduled instalments. Each instalment may include part of the principal and applicable interest. This synthetic text is for retrieval tests only.

documents.title: Test Demo: SACCO Membership
documents.content: SACCO membership describes joining a cooperative and participating as a member. This synthetic overview is not a membership policy and exists only for retrieval testing.

documents.title: Test Demo: Retirement Savings
documents.content: Retirement savings are funds set aside over time to support future needs after employment. This synthetic explanation is not financial advice or an official SACCO document.

documents.title: Test Demo: Becoming a Member
documents.content: A prospective member may be eligible if they meet the cooperative's illustrative age, identification, and common-bond requirements. A sample process is completing a registration form, providing identification, paying a minimum share capital of KES 1,000, and receiving confirmation. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Membership Categories
documents.content: An individual membership is held by one person for personal saving and borrowing. A group or corporate membership is held on behalf of an organised association or business, usually with authorised representatives. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Checking Balance and Statements
documents.content: A member can check an illustrative account balance through an approved mobile channel, USSD menu, branch, or customer support desk. A statement request normally includes the member number and a selected date range, followed by delivery through an approved secure channel. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Updating Personal Details
documents.content: To update a phone number, identification record, address, or next of kin, a member may submit a change request with supporting identification. An illustrative process includes verification by the branch or approved service channel before the record is changed. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Savings Account Types
documents.content: A regular savings account supports routine deposits and permitted withdrawals. A fixed deposit keeps money for an agreed period, while target or goal savings is designed for a defined future purpose. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Minimum Savings Deposits
documents.content: Illustrative minimum opening deposits could be KES 500 for regular savings, KES 5,000 for a fixed deposit, and KES 1,000 for target savings. Actual minimums would be set by the relevant SACCO product terms and may change. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Indicative Savings Interest Rates
documents.content: For illustration, regular savings might earn about 3% per year, while a fixed deposit might earn between 6% and 8% per year depending on its term. Rates are examples for testing retrieval and are not promises, quotations, or official product terms. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Savings Withdrawals
documents.content: Regular savings may allow withdrawals after identity verification, while fixed deposits commonly require maturity or an early-withdrawal request. An illustrative notice period for a target account could be 7 to 30 days, depending on its terms. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Loan Types
documents.content: Illustrative SACCO loan products include development loans for productive projects, emergency loans for urgent needs, school-fees loans for education costs, and asset-finance loans for an approved purchase. Each product can have different limits, security, pricing, and repayment periods. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Loan Eligibility and Multiplier
documents.content: Illustrative eligibility checks may include active membership, regular savings, acceptable repayment history, and sufficient ability to repay. A sample savings multiplier could allow a loan of three to five times qualifying deposits, subject to guarantors and affordability checks. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Loan Rates and Repayment Terms
documents.content: For testing only, a development loan might use a reducing-balance rate near 1.0% per month for up to 36 months, while school-fees lending might use about 1.17% per month for up to 12 months. An emergency loan could use 2% per month for up to 6 months, with terms depending on the product. These illustrative figures are synthetic/demo data, not official rates.

documents.title: Test Demo: Loan Application Documents
documents.content: A sample loan application may require an identification document, recent income evidence, a completed application form, and details of proposed guarantors. Asset finance may also require a quotation, while school-fees lending may require a fee structure. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Loan Guarantorship
documents.content: A guarantor is an eligible member who agrees that their qualifying savings may be considered if the borrower defaults, subject to the applicable agreement. Guarantors commonly review the amount and repayment terms before signing, and release may follow repayment or an approved replacement process. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Dividends
documents.content: Dividends are commonly calculated from a declared rate applied to qualifying share capital for the relevant period. An illustrative annual rate of 8% would produce KES 800 on KES 10,000 of qualifying shares before any applicable adjustments. Declaration and payment depend on audited results and member approval. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Shares and Deposits
documents.content: Share capital represents ownership, may qualify for dividends, and is generally not withdrawable like a deposit. Savings or deposits may earn interest, can be withdrawable under product terms, and may support loan security. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Deposit Channels
documents.content: Illustrative deposit channels include an M-Pesa paybill, bank transfer, approved agent, or branch counter. A member normally keeps the transaction reference and confirms that the account or member number was entered correctly. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Withdrawing Funds
documents.content: A withdrawal request may be made through an approved mobile channel, agent, or branch after identity verification and account checks. Processing time, permitted amount, and whether a notice is required depend on the savings product. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Transaction Limits and Fees
documents.content: Digital transactions may have illustrative daily limits such as KES 50,000, with fees varying by channel and amount. A branch or agent transaction may use a different limit or fee schedule, which should be confirmed before sending funds. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Mobile and USSD Banking
documents.content: Mobile or USSD banking may provide balance checks, deposits, transfers, and selected withdrawal requests after registration and a secure PIN setup. An illustrative access flow is dialling the approved short code, choosing a service, and confirming the transaction. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Deposit Not Reflecting
documents.content: If a deposit does not reflect, a member can keep the receipt or transaction code and check the entered account details. A support request may include the amount, date, channel, sender number, and member number so the transaction can be traced. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Delayed Loan Disbursement
documents.content: For a delayed loan disbursement, a member can confirm whether approval, guarantor signing, security checks, and any required fees are complete. The member can then provide the application reference to the lending desk for a status check. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Complaints and Disputes
documents.content: A complaint or transaction dispute can be submitted with a clear description, relevant dates, supporting references, and a preferred contact method. An illustrative process acknowledges the issue, investigates the records, and communicates an outcome or escalation route. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Escalation Contact Channels
documents.content: Members may use an illustrative branch desk, customer-service phone line, or support email to escalate an unresolved issue. A useful escalation message includes the member number, case reference, a short description, and prior communication details without sharing a PIN. This is synthetic/demo data, not an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Budgeting Basics
documents.content: A simple 50/30/20 framework allocates about 50% of income to needs, 30% to wants, and 20% to saving or debt reduction. For irregular or informal income, a member might base percentages on a conservative average and adjust them in lower-income months. This is synthetic/demo coaching content, not financial advice or an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Consistent Saving and Compounding
documents.content: Regular saving can build a larger balance because new contributions join the money already saved. Compounding means returns may themselves earn future returns, so time and consistency can matter even when individual deposits are small. This is synthetic/demo coaching content, not financial advice or an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Good Debt and Bad Debt
documents.content: Borrowing that supports an income-producing activity or a necessary long-term asset is often described as productive debt, while borrowing for repeated impulse spending can become costly debt. A common responsible-borrowing approach is comparing total repayment with expected benefit and checking that instalments fit variable income. This is synthetic/demo coaching content, not financial advice or an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Emergency Funds
documents.content: An emergency fund can help cover unexpected costs without relying immediately on expensive borrowing. A common educational target is three to six months of essential expenses, built gradually in an accessible savings account before an emergency occurs. This is synthetic/demo coaching content, not financial advice or an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Dividends and Interest
documents.content: Interest is generally a return paid on eligible savings or deposits, while a dividend is a possible distribution linked to ownership through share capital and the cooperative's results. These are different wealth-building levers with different rules, timing, and risk of payment. This is synthetic/demo coaching content, not financial advice or an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Chama and Table-Banking Bridge
documents.content: Chama or table-banking groups can provide a familiar example of members contributing regularly toward shared goals. A common bridge to SACCO saving discipline is keeping a predictable contribution habit while using an account with clear records and individual ownership. This is synthetic/demo coaching content, not financial advice or an official SACCO policy.

documents.title: Test Demo: Basic Investment Literacy
documents.content: Diversification spreads money across different assets so one outcome does not determine the entire result. Risk describes the possibility of loss or changing returns, while time horizon describes how long money can remain invested; these ideas help frame general choices without recommending a specific product. This is synthetic/demo coaching content, not financial advice or an official SACCO policy.
